title: Ba for ball and da for dog are the CDC examples at 15 months
summary: CDC says that by 15 months most children try one or two words besides mama or dada, such as ba for ball or da for dog.
body: The examples on the 15-month CDC sheet are clipped syllables. Ba stands in for ball, and da stands in for dog. The sheet calls these tries, not finished vocabulary items. Mama and dada do not count toward the one or two. A toddler who so far uses only those caregiver names still matches the way the line is written. Most, on this sheet, means at least three quarters of children, so the line is a group mark in the United States, not a rule for every toddler.
